STEP 1 - Scene: This is not really a meal; it is a single whole green pear (or similar green fruit with a stem) resting on a white square plate. The photo is taken from above, nearly straight down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 22-24 cm across its longest diagonal-free width. Taking a side length of about 22 cm, the vessel area is roughly 22 x 22 = 484 cm² (the corners are rounded, so call it ~450 cm²). The pear's width (~6.5 cm across) is consistent with this scale.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole green pear with a stem. No sauce, oil, or other food visible. (Faint reddish streaks on the plate are residue, not food.)

STEP 4 - Area: The pear covers about 6.5 cm x 6.5 cm, roughly 33 cm² in projection, about 7% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: A pear is roughly a sphere-like solid of about 6.5 cm diameter, so volume ≈ (4/3)π(3.25)³ ≈ 145 ml. Treated as a whole piece, the count-based volume is about 145 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole fruit is dense, not a loose bulk pile, so the density is close to water, about 0.9-1.0 g/ml. Weight ≈ 145 × 0.95 ≈ 140 g. This is consistent with a medium pear (typically 130-180 g).

STEP 7 - Energy: Pear, raw, about 57 kcal per 100 g. 140 g × 0.57 ≈ 80 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium pear around 140 g and about 80 kcal is plausible for a single visible fruit. It is far below a full dinner plate, which matches the small share of the plate covered.
